mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in three months indicates a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in two months signals a supply shock, which increases input costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals strong labor demand, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the months where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals a strong demand for housing, which boosts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure under tight monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the same quarter, it signals strong economic growth and labor market tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 2% QoQ and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the quarters where GDPC1 increased by more than 2% and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3%.
